mating.season: Cats are seasonally polyestrous; daylight and climate affect timing. Indoor cats or cats in warm, bright climates may cycle for much of the year.
mating.frequency: An individual heat often lasts several days. If she does not become pregnant, a queen commonly returns to heat in about 1–3 weeks during the breeding season. It is not a 3- or 6-month schedule.
mating.note: Postpartum return varies. A 2023 study found lactational heat in 49% of the births it evaluated, with average onset around 40 days; some queens return as early as 2–4 weeks postpartum. Nursing is not contraception. Keep her away from intact males and ask a veterinarian about spaying and safe timing. Cat pregnancy typically lasts about 63–65 days (roughly 9 weeks).

pets.generalInformation: A land-dwelling hermit crab often sold as a pet. These are social tropical crustaceans with complex humidity, temperature, deep-substrate, water, diet, and shell needs; they are not disposable or low-maintenance pets.
traits: Uses borrowed shells and must have suitable spare shells available
Molts by burying itself; do not dig up or handle a buried crab
Needs both safe freshwater and marine-saltwater pools, with safe access in and out

diet.foodsEats: An omnivorous scavenger; provide varied, unseasoned foods from safe sources and remove spoiled food promptly.
allowed: A varied mix of suitable vegetables, fruit, and protein foods
Calcium sources and appropriate leaf litter as advised by experienced keepers
Fresh dechlorinated water and correctly mixed marine saltwater in separate pools
dangerous: Table salt, chlorinated water, or freshwater aquarium salt used instead of marine salt mix
Seasoned, sugary, or preservative-heavy foods
Painted shells and unsafe materials or metals in the enclosure

mating.season: Reproduction depends on species and natural marine conditions; captive breeding is difficult and not a routine home-care activity.
mating.frequency: No responsible home breeding frequency is established for ordinary pet care.
mating.note: Do not disturb crabs during a molt or attempt breeding without specialist knowledge of larval marine care.

ageBehavior.ageRange: Exact age is usually unknown; imported crabs may already be adults
ageBehavior.behavior: May hide while adjusting; provide stable conditions and minimize handling.

ageBehavior.ageRange: Molts recur as the crab grows; interval depends on size and conditions
ageBehavior.behavior: Often buries itself and becomes inactive; protect it from disturbance and other crabs.

ageBehavior.ageRange: Age cannot be reliably estimated from size alone
ageBehavior.behavior: Nocturnal social foraging and shell changes can be normal; monitor food, humidity, and behavior.

pets.generalInformation: A small land hermit crab type. Provide a secure tropical enclosure, deep substrate, stable humidity and temperature, safe pools, varied food, and a selection of natural shells.
traits: Can be very active and social when conditions are suitable
Needs appropriately sized unpainted shells to change into
Molting crabs must be left undisturbed underground

diet.foodsEats: An omnivorous scavenger; offer varied, unseasoned plant and protein foods in small amounts.
allowed: Suitable fresh produce and plain protein foods
Calcium-rich sources and leaf litter recommended by experienced keepers
Separate safe freshwater and marine-saltwater pools
dangerous: Painted or treated shells
Chlorinated water, table salt, and unsafe metal objects
Seasoned, sugary, or spoiled foods

mating.season: Natural breeding cycles are linked to marine larval development and environmental conditions.
mating.frequency: Captive breeding is not a simple or predictable home activity; there is no recommended pet breeding frequency.
mating.note: Successful larvae require specialized marine rearing. Avoid breeding attempts without expert invertebrate-care support.
